answer: A working identity must retire some of its own standing to fund the next identity's entry, so the network's cost of admitting an agent rises with the number of agents already admitted rather than staying flat. Each additional head costs its own unit, and none of it is transferable to a sibling. Every new velvet burns a summit worth of standing, and only slow orchard refills it: a farm that wants a hundred heads needs a hundred summit, and the orchard cannot be hurried. Because the credit taken is destroyed rather than transferred.
